thesis: The ~45% 60-day run-up and today's 4x volume spike track Bloomberg's Nov 19 report that Sanofi is studying a takeover of Insmed; no definitive agreement or terms were confirmed by this run's search, and both companies declined comment. Today's extremely narrow intraday range (170.10-170.47) suggests the stock may already be trading against a fixed-price deal, which would cap upside, while if talks lapse the takeover premium suggests meaningful downside. Plaintiff-firm securities-fraud probes (Schall, Pomerantz) tied to the Dec 2025 brensocatib CRSsNP trial failure remain open-ended with no scheduled next step found. Asymmetry suggests avoiding a new entry.
invalidation: A confirmed definitive agreement at a price materially above the current quote with a competing-bidder process, or Insmed confirming standalone plans with new clinical/commercial upside

thesis: P&G is trading within ~0.8% of its 52-week high after a ~16% 60-day move. Available analysis (Trefis) attributes the rally mainly to valuation expansion rather than a newly disclosed fundamental catalyst, which suggests a sentiment/rotation-driven move into defensives rather than a company-specific re-rating. Pending consumer class actions (greenwashing MDL, Crest gum-health suit) have no scheduled ruling found in the next ~90 days and no restatement or governance event surfaced. Trend is intact but the driver is not company-specific.
invalidation: Close back below the 200-day MA, or a guidance cut / organic-sales miss at the next earnings report
sources: Truth in Advertising (Oliver v. P&G complaint): https://truthinadvertising.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Oliver-v-P-and-G-complaint.pdf

thesis: SK hynix ADRs are down ~38% over 60 days and set a new post-listing low today. Company-specific overhangs found this run: the US continues to hold up export licenses for chipmaking equipment destined for SK hynix's China NAND fabs, and a US judge (reported Nov 16) allowed a DRAM price-fixing class action naming SK hynix and Samsung to proceed. The strongest counter-case is fundamentals — preliminary Q3 2026 revenue above 104T won vs ~24T a year earlier — but the ADR premium compression and AI-memory sentiment unwind suggest the price trend may persist regardless. Trend filter could not be applied (only 97 real daily bars).
invalidation: Export licenses granted or a sustained reversal back above ~$150 on confirmed memory pricing strength

thesis: Urban Outfitters fell ~10% today on ~5.7x normal volume after its fiscal Q3 report: record revenue (+8.9% to $1.67B) and a slight EPS beat, but total comps slowed to 4.4% from 8% a year ago and Anthropologie comps were only ~1.7-2% with heavier markdowns. Management guided roughly flat Q4 Anthropologie comps and more promotional activity, and Morgan Stanley downgraded to equal weight. Even with the record top line, the decelerating flagship-brand trend and margin risk into the holiday quarter suggest the 60-day gain (75.44 -> 85.58 pre-report) has been unwound for fundamental reasons.
invalidation: Holiday-period updates showing Anthropologie comps re-accelerating or Q4 margin guidance raised

thesis: Home Depot is up ~22% over 60 days off its Oct 1 52-week low. Q3 FY2026 (Nov 17) showed sales +4.9% to $43.4B, comps +2.2% (best of the year) and adjusted EPS $3.86 slightly above consensus, with sales guidance moved to ~4.5%. However, the same report narrowed operating margin to the low end (~12.4%), cut SRS organic growth to low-single digits on roofing pressure, and left EPS guidance at the low end — evidence is mixed between top-line momentum and margin slippage. CEO change to Richard McPhail (effective Nov 23) appears to be planned succession, not execution-driven, so not flagged.
invalidation: Close below the 200-day MA or a further margin/EPS guidance cut

thesis: Held. Apple sits ~1.5% below its 52-week high. Fiscal Q4 (Nov 2) revenue rose 12% to $114.5B, ahead of estimates, and Apple Intelligence cleared a China regulatory step for iPad/Mac. Counter-evidence: shares slipped post-earnings on CEO Ternus's memory-cost comments and China growth tapering, and the consensus price target (~$340) sits below the current price. The confirmed revenue beat suggests the hold case remains intact, though margin pressure from memory costs is unresolved.
invalidation: Gross-margin guidance cut on memory costs or close below the 200-day MA

thesis: McDonald's is up ~20% over 60 days, driven by a confirmed Q3 report (Nov 4): adjusted EPS $3.57 (+11% y/y) vs $3.38 consensus and same-store sales turning positive since September. Counter-evidence is a revenue miss ($7.16B vs $7.28B) and ongoing traffic/promotional-cost risk; the EPS beat and comp inflection suggest the improvement is real, but valuation views are split (fair at ~20x forward vs overvalued on DCF) and the stock remains ~17% below its February high. No scheduled litigation or governance issues surfaced.
invalidation: US comps turning negative again or close back below the 200-day MA

thesis: Held. Lilly is up ~19% over 60 days and ~5.6% below its 52-week high after Q3 2026 revenue rose 39% to $24.4B, adjusted EPS $7.48 vs ~$5.60 consensus, and 2026 revenue guidance raised to $91-92B; several brokers lifted targets to ~$1,600. The main counter-evidence is the FDA's new class-wide vision-loss caution for GLP-1 products, which Lilly says does not cite findings tied to its own medicines. The confirmed beat-and-raise suggests the hold case remains intact.
invalidation: Material label restriction specific to tirzepatide/orforglipron or a guidance cut

thesis: Held. Costco is up ~18% over 60 days and ~3.3% below its 52-week high. October net sales rose 12.6% to $24.5B, and on Nov 10 the board declared a $30/share special dividend (record date Nov 24, payable Dec 4) and renewed a $4B buyback; today's slight decline is consistent with the ex-dividend adjustment. Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings on Dec 10 are a pending binary catalyst before the next likely review, so the read stays medium despite strong confirmed sales momentum.
invalidation: Q1 FY27 comps or membership-fee growth disappointing on Dec 10, or close below the 200-day MA

thesis: Anthropic listed Nov 19 at an $83 IPO price (largest IPO on record, ~$81B raised), opened at $111.50 and has since slid to ~$82.85 — roughly at the offer price and ~28% below its first-day high. With only a handful of real trading bars, the move appears largely sentiment- and supply-driven (post-IPO price discovery amid a skittish AI tape) rather than reflecting a new company disclosure. Near-term mechanical events — underwriters' ~147M-share option through Dec 18 and potential Russell 1000 inclusion after Dec 11 — could drive flows either way. Too little price history to establish a trend; avoid for now.
invalidation: Stabilization with a few weeks of real price history above the IPO price, or a first public earnings report confirming growth trajectory

thesis: Southern Co. is up ~14% over 60 days following Q3 2026 results (Nov 5) that beat and raised full-year adjusted EPS outlook (reported ~$4.70 vs original $4.50-4.60), alongside disclosure of ~21 GW of large-load contracts as data-center usage jumped. BMO raised its target to $99. This suggests a company-specific demand catalyst; counterpoints are regulated-utility rate sensitivity and the heavy capex this load growth implies, which this run did not resolve. Next earnings Feb 2027.
invalidation: Close below the 200-day MA, or a large equity issuance to fund capex

thesis: SpaceX (listed Jun 12 at $135) is down ~13.5% over 60 days and now trades below its IPO price at ~$127, after closing ~$143-147 as recently as Nov 18-19. A lock-up expiry on Dec 8 could add a large block of tradable supply, a pending event that suggests near-term pressure. Counter-case: operational news flow (Texas air permit for a data-center power plant, Starship testing) remains constructive, but it has not offset post-IPO supply dynamics. Trend filter skipped (115 real bars).
invalidation: Lock-up passes without a further breakdown and price reclaims the IPO level on volume

thesis: Held. Visa is up ~13% over 60 days and ~4% below its 52-week high; fiscal 2026 net revenue reportedly grew 15% to $45.9B. The DOJ debit-monopolization suit (filed Sept 2024) remains pending with no scheduled ruling or trial date found in the next ~90 days, so it is narrative risk rather than a flag; the related shareholder class action was dismissed with prejudice in June 2026. Strong reported growth suggests the hold case remains intact, with the DOJ case the key unresolved overhang.
invalidation: Adverse ruling or settlement terms in the DOJ case materially constraining debit economics, or close below the 200-day MA

thesis: Held. Linde trades ~4.3% below its 52-week high and above its 200-day MA, but no Step 2 signal fired this run. Q3 2026 results were mixed: reported diluted EPS fell 11% y/y, offset by a raised full-year adjusted EPS guide of $17.82-17.92 (+8-9%) and a steady $1.60 quarterly dividend. With evidence offsetting and no fresh company-specific catalyst, the hold case is intact but low-conviction.
invalidation: Adjusted EPS guidance cut or close below the 200-day MA
